paragraphs: The morning can begin with blood-pressure checks and salt-reduction education for older adults. In the afternoon, the worker visits a resident living alone, records an abnormal blood-glucose result, and refers the person to a community health center. At dusk, the worker sends health reminders, summarizes the day's outreach, and prepares for the next screening event.

In short, Community health workers bring health services to residents' doors. They educate, follow up, conduct outreach, maintain records, make referrals, and organize programs. The role is the access hub of frontline health services.

Community health workers emphasize prevention, education, follow-up, and referrals in neighborhoods. Medical social workers coordinate social resources and crisis intervention in health-care settings. One prevents illness in the community; the other addresses urgent needs around clinical care, and the roles often collaborate.

AI will not replace the occupation as a whole, but it will accelerate education and reminders.
